Chubb trades at reasonable multiples (12.5x trailing P/E, 2.73 PEG) with solid underwriting margins (17.9%) and improving momentum. Modest leverage (20.9x D/E) and steady 8.3% revenue growth support a high-conviction long despite low ROE (14.2%).

Parker Hannifin shows strong earnings growth (18.6%) and solid 6m momentum (18.6%), but forward P/E of 23.3x and elevated D/E (74x) suggest mixed valuation. ROE of 27.4% and healthy operating margins (25.4%) keep it watchlist-worthy.

Marsh McLennan offers good revenue growth (8.2%) and exceptional ROE (39.4%), but extremely high D/E (132.7x) and expensive forward P/E (22.2x) are red flags. Missing gross margin data limits conviction despite strong cash generation.

Intercontinental Exchange has attractive PEG (1.86) and solid 6m momentum (11.8%), but trailing P/E of 35.8x is steep for modest 7.3% revenue growth. Low ROE (9.9%) and missing gross margin data weaken the case despite strong 34.1% operating margins.

Becton Dickinson is a value trap: low P/E (12.8x forward, 26.5x trailing) obscures weak fundamentals—minimal earnings growth (2.2%), tepid revenue growth (3.8%), and ROE of only 4.8%. Decent free cash flow cannot offset deteriorating fundamentals.

Emerson Electric delivers strong earnings growth (28.3%) and revenue growth (16.1%) with solid 6m momentum (17.4%). Forward P/E of 20x and PEG of 2.09 are reasonable; 17.1% ROE and 20% operating margins support conviction despite higher beta (1.15).

Marathon Petroleum is a broken value trap: negative earnings growth (-39.7%), negative revenue growth (-7.7%), and deteriorating fundamentals offset cheap 11.5x forward P/E. Thin 2.7% profit margins and cyclical energy headwinds make this a clear avoid.

Adobe is a quality long with exceptional gross margins (89.5%), ROE (46.2%), and strong operating margins (35.1%); PEG of 1.3 is compelling. Negative 1m momentum (-4.5%) is a minor concern, but fundamentals and FCF generation (7.6B) support the thesis.

Stryker has solid revenue and earnings growth (10.7%, 14.7%) with 6m momentum of 7.7%, but trailing P/E of 38.5x is expensive relative to 14.7% profit margins and 18.9% ROE. PEG of 2.52 and 26.7x forward P/E suggest limited upside.

Duke Energy is a defensive play undermined by excessive leverage (161.5x D/E), negative free cash flow (-1.9B), and weak earnings growth (3.6%). High payout ratio (69%) limits reinvestment; utility qualities insufficient to offset balance-sheet stress.

Equinix is a value trap: 78.96x trailing P/E and 37.2x forward P/E are indefensible despite 26.5% earnings growth. Negative FCF (-1.1B), payout ratio >2x, excessive leverage (138.7x D/E), and low ROE (5%) disqualify this REIT.

Colgate-Palmolive offers stable quality with 59% gross margins and 20% operating margins, plus 10.6% earnings growth. Missing debt/equity and ROE data limits confidence, but 21.1x forward P/E and 2.75 PEG provide reasonable entry for a defensive compounder.

Aon shows strong revenue growth (17.4%) and earnings growth (18.3%) with solid 6m momentum (11.3%), but D/E of 295x is dangerously high for an insurance broker. Forward P/E of 22.3x and missing ROE data add uncertainty to conviction.

Mondelez has deteriorating fundamentals: negative earnings growth (-14.5%) and weak 6m momentum (-5.6%) outweigh low P/E of 16.2x. Modest revenue growth (3.5%), moderate FCF, and 12.5% ROE cannot offset earnings headwinds.

Amphenol delivers exceptional revenue growth (35%) and earnings growth (30.2%) with strong 6m momentum (19%). Forward P/E of 32.2x is steep, but PEG of 2.86 and ROE of 28.9% support watchlist status; 1m negative momentum is a minor caveat.

KLA shows exceptional fundamentals: 36.8% profit margins, 112% ROE, and 24.2% revenue growth with strong PEG (1.37). Forward P/E of 20.1x is reasonable; 6m momentum (2.6%) is modest but solid FCF (2.6B) and operating leverage justify high-conviction thesis.

Waste Management has steady fundamentals (42.5% ROE, 16.2% revenue growth) but valuation is stretched: 28.2x forward P/E and 3.77 PEG signal overpricing for 2.1% earnings growth. Excessive leverage (165.9x D/E) and high payout (54%) limit upside.

Moody's has strong fundamentals: 30.2% profit margins, 18.5% earnings growth, and solid 6m momentum (14.4%). Forward P/E of 29x is elevated, but PEG of 2.56 and 40.2% operating margins justify watchlist. Missing D/E and ROE data cap conviction.

Trane Technologies delivers impressive 31.9% earnings growth and 13% revenue growth with exceptional 6m momentum (24.7%). Forward P/E of 27.6x is fair given PEG of 2.69 and 30% ROE; solid free cash flow and moderate D/E (57.5x) support high-conviction long.

Welltower has solid revenue growth (16.5%) and exceptional earnings growth (29.3%), but REIT structure shows red flags: 35.8x forward P/E, 75.5x trailing P/E, 4.0 PEG, and payout ratio >1.6x are unsustainable. Missing FCF and low 5.2% ROE are disqualifying.

PayPal offers compelling valuation (14.6x forward P/E, 0.8 PEG) and strong FCF (6.3B), plus 6m momentum of 13%. However, minimal revenue growth (1.3%) and tepid 9.8% earnings growth dampen conviction. High beta (1.54) requires discipline.

Cintas is a quality compounder (40.5% ROE, 11.3% earnings growth) with decent FCF and 6m momentum (10.4%), but valuation is prohibitive: 40.5x forward P/E and 3.88 PEG leave minimal margin of safety. Watchlist pending pullback.

Illinois Tool Works has solid fundamentals (21.6% profit margins, 28.9% operating margins) and reasonable P/E (20.98x forward), but slow growth (2.7% revenue, 6.9% earnings) limits upside. Missing D/E and ROE data and high payout (56.5%) cap conviction.

Constellation Energy shows strong 6m momentum (24.4%) and solid profit margins (22.3%), plus positive 7.9% revenue growth. Forward P/E of 19.5x is attractive; negative earnings growth (-2.5%) is offset by utility stability and improving technical setup.

PNC Financial offers compelling valuation (12.4x forward P/E) and exceptional 6m momentum (19.9%), with solid 29% profit margins. Missing gross margin, operating margin, ROE, and FCF data limit conviction. Modest 5.6% earnings growth restrains upside.
